_about: How the Core assistant interprets a scheduled-maintenance milestone for the advisor: which tier each item belongs to (by PreferredTerm, or Component when there is none), what to call it to the customer, why it matters, and what skipping it risks. tiers are in the order the advisor should bring them up. recommend: true tiers are what 'Add recommended' adds. inspectionGroups names the systems the bundled multi-point inspection covers, by keyword in the check's name. Wording is customer-facing: plain, no pressure, no claims beyond the schedule.

tiers.label: Safety
tiers.say: These affect how the vehicle stops, steers and grips the road.

tiers.label: Protects the engine
tiers.say: These keep the engine and drivetrain from wearing early; skipping them costs more later.

tiers.label: Comfort and efficiency
tiers.say: These are nice to keep up but can wait if the customer wants to keep today's bill down.

engine oil.why: Fresh oil keeps the engine's moving parts from wearing.
engine oil.skip: Old oil breaks down and can sludge, which is how engines wear out early.

engine oil filter.why: Fresh oil keeps the engine's moving parts from wearing.
engine oil filter.skip: Old oil breaks down and can sludge, which is how engines wear out early.

spark plug.why: Worn plugs cause misfires, rough running and worse fuel economy.
spark plug.skip: Misfires can damage the catalytic converter, which is an expensive part.

engine coolant.why: Coolant wears out and stops protecting against corrosion inside the engine.
engine coolant.skip: Old coolant corrodes the water pump and radiator from the inside.

transmission fluid.why: Clean fluid keeps shifts smooth and the transmission cool.
transmission fluid.skip: Worn fluid is a common reason transmissions fail early.

differential fluid.why: It lubricates the gears that drive the wheels.
differential fluid.skip: Worn fluid lets the gears wear and whine.

transfer case fluid.skip: Worn fluid wears the all-wheel-drive system.

drive belt.why: The belt runs the alternator, A/C and water pump.
drive belt.skip: A broken belt can leave the customer stranded.

vacuum pump.why: It supplies the power assist for the brakes on this engine.
vacuum pump.skip: A failing pump makes the brake pedal hard to push.

battery.why: A weak battery is the most common reason a car will not start.
battery.skip: It tends to fail on the first cold morning.

high voltage battery air filter.why: It keeps the hybrid battery cool.
high voltage battery air filter.skip: A clogged filter makes the hybrid battery run hot and wear out faster.

FUEL ADDITIVE.skip: Deposits build slowly and can hurt fuel economy.

tires.why: Rotating evens out wear so the tires grip evenly and last longer.
tires.skip: Uneven wear shortens tire life and can affect handling in the rain.

disc brake pad.skip: Worn-out pads damage the rotors and lengthen stopping distance.

brake system.why: It catches worn parts before they affect stopping.
brake system.skip: Brake problems get more expensive the longer they go.

window wiper blade.skip: Streaking blades make it hard to see in bad weather.

cabin air filter.why: It cleans the air coming through the vents and keeps the A/C blowing strong.
cabin air filter.skip: A clogged one means weak airflow and a musty smell.

engine air filter.why: A clean filter helps fuel economy and performance.
engine air filter.skip: A dirty one slowly costs fuel economy.

fuel cap seal.why: A bad seal can turn on the check engine light.
fuel cap seal.skip: It can set off the check engine light.
